newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit pressured by dollar bids, but fall limited.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit pressured by dollar bids, but fall limited.

text.p: The ringgit weakened on strong dollar bids amid rumours that Bank Negara would be holding meetings with local bank heads to discuss some possible restriction on ringgit lending to offshore players, dealers said on Friday.
They said both local and offshore players were quick to react to the rumour, hitting both the spot and forward market in good size.
"Some U.S. and Swiss names were seen as main buyers of dollar/ringgit and forward swaps," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
Bank Negara could not be reached for comment. It also does not comment on its open market operations.
But the ringgit's weakness was again limited to 2.5250, the level which Bank Negara is widely expected to defend.
The central bank was said to have placed orders to sell the dollar at 2.5250, dealers said.
Bank Negara was believed to have sold an estimated $300 million on Thursday in defence of the ringgit.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5244/54 to a dollar. It closed at 2.5240/50 in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.
Dollar/ringgit fell to a low of 2.5140/50 during London trading overnight as offshore players who were long on spot ringgit were forced to cover their positions after a jump in swap rates.
Swaps had fallen back, probably on unwinding of long positions by speculators who fear that Bank Negara may pre-empt their plans of hitting the ringgit, dealers said.
They said with New York on holiday, further advances in dollar/ringit were unlikely.
